canh-ga-nau-khoai-tay.name: Vietnamese Chicken and Potato Soup
aliases: Chicken Soup with Potatoes and Carrots
canh-ga-nau-khoai-tay.serving_basis: One pot of soup for four people to share with rice.
canh-ga-nau-khoai-tay.description: Chicken simmered with potatoes, carrots, and onion makes a mild, naturally sweet broth. It is a comforting hot soup with vegetables for an everyday family meal.
canh-ga-nau-khoai-tay.finished_dish: The chicken is tender and fully cooked; the potatoes and carrots are soft but hold their shape. The clear broth tastes gently sweet and is seasoned lightly.
canh-ga-nau-khoai-tay.serving: Ladle into a bowl while hot, finish with scallions, cilantro, and a little pepper, and serve with steamed rice.
tips: Bone-in thighs or wings give the broth more flavor.
Add the potatoes a few minutes after the carrots so both vegetables finish cooking without falling apart.
Skim the broth as it first boils to keep it clear; add fish sauce near the end for a fresher aroma.
search_terms: chicken soup with potatoes and carrots
canh-ga-nau-khoai-tay.image_alt: A bowl of Vietnamese chicken and potato soup with carrots, onion, scallions, and clear golden broth.
canh-ga-nau-khoai-tay.time_note: About 50 minutes; cooking time varies with the size of the chicken pieces and vegetables.
ingredients: Cut into serving pieces; pat dry with a paper towel if wet, and do not rinse raw chicken under running water.
Peel and cut into chunks; keep in water to prevent browning.
Peel and cut into slices about 1 cm thick.
Replace part with unsalted chicken stock if desired.
For sauteing the shallot and chicken.
Optional if using already seasoned stock.
preparation_steps: Cut the chicken into serving pieces; pat it dry with a paper towel if wet, and do not rinse raw chicken under running water. Peel the potatoes and carrots and cut them into similar-sized pieces. Use separate tools for raw poultry and clean them after handling.
Chop the shallot and cut the onion into wedges. Slice the scallions and cilantro, keeping them aside for finishing.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil in a pot and saute the shallot until fragrant. Add the chicken and cook, turning, until the surfaces are firm.
Add the water and bring it to a boil, skimming off foam. Reduce to a steady simmer and cook for about 15 minutes, until the chicken is nearly done.
Add the carrot and simmer for about 5 minutes, then add the potatoes. Continue until the chicken is fully cooked and the vegetables are just tender.

Add the onion and season with salt, seasoning powder, and fish sauce. Simmer for a few minutes, taste, then turn off the heat and finish with scallions, cilantro, and pepper. Use a food thermometer to confirm the thickest piece reaches 74°C (165°F) before serving.
canh-ga-nau-khoai-tay.media_alt_text: A bowl of chicken and potato soup with carrot, onion and scallions in a clear golden broth.

ga-kho-tieu.name: Vietnamese Braised Chicken with Black Pepper
ga-kho-tieu.serving_basis: One braised chicken dish to share with rice among four people.
ga-kho-tieu.description: Chicken is seared and gently braised with fish sauce, caramel, and black pepper. The balanced savory-sweet sauce is warmly aromatic and pairs well with rice and boiled greens.
ga-kho-tieu.finished_dish: The chicken is tender but still holds to the bone, and a lightly thickened sauce coats each piece. Black pepper is distinct without overpowering the chicken.
ga-kho-tieu.serving: Serve hot in a shallow dish, finished with scallions and freshly ground pepper, alongside steamed rice.
tips: Marinate the chicken for at least 20 minutes so it absorbs the shallot, pepper, and fish sauce.
Searing the chicken before braising helps the pieces stay firm and adds flavor to the sauce.
Add small amounts of hot water if the sauce reduces before the chicken is tender.
search_terms: Vietnamese braised chicken with black pepper
ga-kho-tieu.image_alt: A dish of Vietnamese braised chicken in a glossy amber pepper sauce with scallions.
ga-kho-tieu.time_note: About 70 minutes including a 20-minute marinade; braising time depends on the cut and size of the pieces.
ingredients: Cut into serving pieces; pat dry with a paper towel if wet, and do not rinse raw chicken under running water.
Peel and slice or finely chop.
Use part for the marinade and the rest during braising.
Use just enough for a light amber color.
Season lightly because the fish sauce is salty.
Add gradually during braising if needed.
Optional; remove the seeds for milder heat.
preparation_steps: Cut the chicken into serving pieces; pat it dry if wet, and do not rinse raw chicken under running water. Lightly crush the peppercorns, slice the shallot, and finely slice the scallions. Use separate tools for raw poultry, then wash your hands and clean the utensils.
Marinate the chicken with the shallot, about 20 ml of fish sauce, half the pepper, and a little salt for 20 minutes.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil in a pot or deep skillet. Sear the chicken on both sides until the surfaces begin to firm, then pour off excess oil if necessary.
Add the remaining fish sauce, sugar, and caramel sauce; turn the chicken to coat. Pour in the hot water, cover, and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low and braise for about 25–30 minutes. Turn gently from time to time and add a little hot water if the sauce reduces before the chicken is tender.

Taste and adjust the savory-sweet balance. Uncover and simmer until the sauce lightly coats the chicken. Turn off the heat and add the remaining pepper and scallions. Use a food thermometer to confirm the thickest piece reaches 74°C (165°F) before serving.
ga-kho-tieu.media_alt_text: Chicken braised with black pepper in a glossy golden-brown sauce and finished with scallions.

ga-xao-thom-bong-cai.name: Vietnamese Chicken Stir-Fry with Pineapple and Broccoli
aliases: Chicken Stir-Fried with Pineapple and Broccoli
Vietnamese Chicken with Broccoli and Pineapple
ga-xao-thom-bong-cai.serving_basis: One stir-fried platter to share among four people.
ga-xao-thom-bong-cai.description: Chicken is stir-fried with green and white broccoli, pineapple, and bell pepper for a gently sweet, lightly tart dish with crisp vegetables. Serve it hot with steamed rice.
ga-xao-thom-bong-cai.finished_dish: The chicken is tender, both types of broccoli remain lightly crisp, and the pineapple is just warmed through. A lightly thickened sauce coats the ingredients without pooling on the plate.
ga-xao-thom-bong-cai.serving: Arrange on a wide platter, finish with scallions, cilantro, and pepper, and serve while hot.
tips: A little cornstarch in the marinade helps the chicken retain moisture during a quick stir-fry.
Briefly blanch and drain the broccoli so it keeps its color and releases less water in the pan.
Add the pineapple near the end so its pieces stay intact and the sauce does not turn too tart.
search_terms: Vietnamese chicken stir-fry with pineapple and broccoli
ga-xao-thom-bong-cai.image_alt: A platter of chicken stir-fried with pineapple, green and white broccoli, and red bell pepper.
ga-xao-thom-bong-cai.time_note: About 30 minutes; blanch the broccoli briefly so it stays crisp during stir-frying.
ingredients: Cut into small florets and rinse.
Cut into small florets and rinse.
Peel, remove the eyes, and cut into bite-size pieces.
Remove seeds and cut into squares.
Use part to marinate the chicken and the rest to season the pan.
Vegetarian oyster sauce may be used if needed.
Use half in the marinade and whisk the rest into water for the sauce.
Whisk with the remaining cornstarch to make a light sauce.
preparation_steps: Slice the chicken into bite-size pieces. Marinate with 8 ml of soy sauce, half the cornstarch, and a little pepper for 10 minutes.
Separate the broccoli and cauliflower into small florets, rinse, then briefly blanch in boiling water. Drain well; cut the pineapple and bell pepper into bite-size pieces.
Finely chop the garlic and ginger; slice the scallions and cilantro. Whisk the remaining cornstarch with the water.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil and briefly saute the garlic and ginger until fragrant. Add the chicken and stir-fry over medium heat until firm and nearly cooked through.
Add both kinds of broccoli, a splash of water, the remaining soy sauce, and the oyster sauce. Toss until the vegetables are just tender.
Add the pineapple and bell pepper. Slowly pour in the cornstarch mixture, stirring until the sauce lightly coats the ingredients.

Taste and add a little sugar if the pineapple is tart. Turn off the heat once the chicken is fully cooked, fold in the scallions and cilantro, and serve hot. Use a food thermometer to confirm the thickest piece reaches 74°C (165°F) before serving.
ga-xao-thom-bong-cai.media_alt_text: Chicken stir-fried with pineapple, broccoli, cauliflower and red bell pepper on a plate.

thit-ngan-om-sau.name: Vietnamese Muscovy Duck Braised with Dracontomelon
aliases: Vietnamese Duck and Sour Dracontomelon Stew
thit-ngan-om-sau.serving_basis: One pot of braised duck for four people, served with rice or rice noodles.
thit-ngan-om-sau.description: Muscovy duck simmers gently with dracontomelon, ginger, and lemongrass until tender. The broth is lightly sour and aromatic, making a warming family dish, especially when dracontomelon is in season.
thit-ngan-om-sau.finished_dish: The duck is tender yet holds its shape, and the broth is fragrant with ginger and lemongrass. The dracontomelon is pressed just enough to give a gentle tartness.
thit-ngan-om-sau.serving: Finish with scallions and Vietnamese coriander; serve hot with steamed rice or rice noodles.
tips: Rub the duck with salt and ginger, then rinse well to reduce its natural aroma.
Marinating and searing the duck before simmering help the seasoning cling to the meat and deepen the broth.
Press the dracontomelon one fruit at a time and taste between additions to control the tartness.
search_terms: Vietnamese muscovy duck braised with dracontomelon
Vietnamese duck and sour dracontomelon stew
duck braised with Vietnamese sour fruit
thit-ngan-om-sau.image_alt: A bowl of Vietnamese muscovy duck braised with green dracontomelon fruit, scallions, and Vietnamese coriander.
thit-ngan-om-sau.time_note: About 85 minutes including a 25-minute marinade; tenderness varies with the size and age of the duck.
ingredients: Cut into serving pieces; pat dry with a paper towel if wet, and do not rinse raw duck under running water.
Scrape clean, rinse, and lightly score the skin.
Use some in the cleaning rub and finely chop the rest.
Bruise two stalks; finely chop the remainder.
Use for the marinade and final seasoning.
Use less if the dracontomelon is mild.
For aromatics and searing the duck.
Add enough to nearly cover the duck.
preparation_steps: Pat the duck dry with a paper towel if wet; do not rinse raw duck under running water. Cut it into serving pieces on a separate board, then wash your hands and clean the knife and board.
Scrape and lightly score the dracontomelon. Finely chop the shallot, garlic, ginger, and some of the lemongrass; bruise the remaining lemongrass.
Marinate the duck with the chopped aromatics, salt, and sugar for about 20–25 minutes. Finely slice the scallions and Vietnamese coriander.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil in a pot and saute the shallot, garlic, and lemongrass until fragrant. Add the marinated duck and cook until the pieces are seared and aromatic.
Add the water and bruised lemongrass. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer, partially covered, for about 25 minutes.
Add the dracontomelon and simmer for about 15 minutes more, or until the duck is tender. Press the fruits one at a time into the broth, taste for tartness, and season with fish sauce.

Turn off the heat when the sour and savory flavors are balanced. Finish with scallions and Vietnamese coriander; serve hot with rice or noodles. Use a food thermometer to confirm the thickest piece reaches 74°C (165°F) before serving.
thit-ngan-om-sau.media_alt_text: Muscovy duck gently braised with dracontomelon fruit, scallions and sawtooth coriander in a bowl.

bun-ngan-mang.name: Vietnamese Rice Noodle Soup with Muscovy Duck and Bamboo Shoots
aliases: Duck vermicelli soup with fresh bamboo shoots
bun-ngan-mang.serving_basis: Four bowls of rice noodles with duck broth and bamboo shoots.
bun-ngan-mang.description: Muscovy duck is simmered to make a fragrant broth, then served with fresh rice vermicelli and bamboo shoots that have been boiled thoroughly. Slice the duck separately so every bowl gets meat and greens.
bun-ngan-mang.finished_dish: The hot broth is lightly aromatic with ginger and lemongrass; the duck is tender, the bamboo shoots are free of their raw pungency, and the noodles remain springy.
bun-ngan-mang.serving: Divide noodles among bowls, top with sliced duck and bamboo shoots, then ladle over hot broth. Serve with ginger-garlic fish sauce and fresh herbs if desired.
tips: Boil fresh bamboo shoots uncovered for 2–3 rounds, discarding the water after each round before adding them to the broth.
Keep the duck at a gentle simmer and check that the thickest piece is fully cooked before removing it.
Season the broth after the bamboo shoots have simmered in it so the final salt level stays balanced.

Muscovy duck and bamboo-shoot noodle soup
duck soup with fresh bamboo shoots

bun-ngan-mang.time_note: About 85 minutes; larger or older duck may need longer to become tender.
ingredients: Pat dry with a paper towel if wet; do not rinse raw duck under running water.
Slice or shred; boil thoroughly and discard the cooking water.
Briefly blanch in boiling water and drain.

preparation_steps: Pat the duck dry with a paper towel if wet; do not rinse raw duck under running water. Use a separate knife and board, then wash your hands and clean the utensils. Bruise the lemongrass and shallot; slice the ginger.

Slice or shred the fresh bamboo shoots. Boil them uncovered with a little salt for about 5 minutes after the water boils, then discard the water. Repeat with fresh water 1–2 more times, rinse, and drain.
Rinse and slice the herbs and scallions. Prepare the rice vermicelli and mix fish sauce with garlic, lime, sugar, and chili to taste for dipping.
cooking_steps: Put the duck in a pot with the water, lemongrass, ginger, and shallot. Bring to a boil, skim the foam, then reduce to a gentle simmer for about 45–55 minutes, depending on the thickness of the meat.
Pierce the thickest part to check doneness. Once fully cooked, remove the duck, let it cool slightly, and cut it into serving pieces.
Add the prepared bamboo shoots to the broth and simmer for about 15 minutes. Season with fish sauce, salt, and seasoning powder; skim some fat if a lighter broth is preferred.

Briefly blanch the noodles in boiling water and divide them among bowls. Add duck, bamboo shoots, and herbs, then ladle over hot broth and serve with ginger-garlic fish sauce. Use a food thermometer to confirm the thickest piece reaches 74°C (165°F) before serving.
